title: How India Elects Its President

endcard.line: Pictures: Beohar Rammanohar Sinha; David Castor (public domain); MohitSingh (CC BY 3.0)

segments.say: India's President isn't chosen by the people directly, or by Parliament alone. The vote is shared between Delhi and the states.

anim.title: Who votes (Article 54)
items: Elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry

segments.say: The voters are an electoral college: the elected members of both Houses of Parliament, and the elected members of every state assembly, plus Delhi and Puducherry.
Nominated members don't vote, and neither do members of state legislative councils.

anim.title: Not every vote is equal
items: An MLA's vote is weighted by the state's population
A big state's MLA counts for more
All MPs together equal all MLAs together

segments.say: Here's the twist. Each MLA's vote carries a value based on the state's population, and MPs' votes are set so that Parliament and the states carry equal weight.

anim.title: How the count works
items: Winner needs more than half the value
If no one has it, the lowest is dropped
Their votes move to the next choice

segments.say: Voters rank the candidates. To win, you need more than half the total value. If no one gets it, the last candidate drops out and their votes pass on. This is the single transferable vote, by secret ballot.
The term is five years. A President can be removed only by impeachment for violation of the Constitution, by both Houses.

anim.title: For your answer
items: Art. 55: proportional representation, single transferable vote

segments.say: For GS Two: Article fifty-four, the electoral college. Article fifty-five, the single transferable vote. Article sixty-one, impeachment.

sources: Constitution of India, Articles 54 (electoral college; Explanation added by the 70th Amendment, 1992, including Delhi and Puducherry), 55 (manner of election: value of votes, proportional representation by single transferable vote, secret ballot), 56 (term), 61 (impeachment)
Election Commission of India, 'Presidential Election' handbook: nominated members and legislative council members do not vote; quota of more than half the valid votes' value
NCERT Class 11, 'Indian Constitution at Work', ch. 4 (Executive)

quiz.q: Who does NOT vote in the presidential election?

quiz.why: Proportional representation by single transferable vote, Article 55.

quiz.q: What makes an MLA's vote value differ between states?
